title: Mirror codebook for multiple neural functions
hypothesis: When many functions share clustered latent states in a fixed neural decoder, a compact learned codebook plus per-function addresses reduces actual decoder-plus-code bytes while preserving held-out function quality and interpolation better than unconstrained DeepSDF latent vectors.
physical_object: One fixed shared neural coordinate decoder mapping x∈R² and latent z∈R⁸ through a 2→32→8 tanh feature MLP and feature/latent inner product.
mirror_coordinate: Eight learned codebook vectors in R⁸ and one uint8 codebook address per function; codebook trained only on training functions.
logical_multiplicity: 128 distinct neural functions from one shared decoder: 64 training functions and 64 held-out functions across four private-residual levels.
controls: unconstrained DeepSDF latent vector per function (8 FP16 values)
rank-4 PCA latent basis with four per-function coefficients (native low-rank control)
nearest-centroid vector quantization using the same eight-entry codebook (algebraically equivalent native codebook control)

task.decoder: Fixed random seeded neural coordinate decoder φθ(x)·z, with φθ(x)=tanh(W2 tanh(W1x+b1)+b2); identical frozen θ in all methods.
task.target_codes: Each target latent is one of eight random prototypes plus Gaussian private residual at the declared standard deviation; prototypes are shared across train and held-out functions but held-out task residuals are independent.
task.interpolation: Average pairs of held-out task codes and reconstruct the midpoint function; report by residual level.

development.codebook_fit: K-means on training-task latents inferred only from training support queries; 50 iterations.
development.selection_metric: held-out query NRMSE, 50/50 interpolation NRMSE and actual serialized payload bytes by residual level.

storage.format: deterministic NPZ with FP16 decoder/codebook/basis/latent tensors, uint8 addresses and metadata
paid_objects: all codebook vectors or PCA basis

compute.report: Include per-task support-query latent fitting and assignment search separately from stored-code inference.

success_gate: On both development seeds at residual std 0 and 0.05, codebook held-out NRMSE <=0.05, <=DeepSDF NRMSE, interpolation NRMSE <=0.10, and actual payload <=0.80x DeepSDF. Passing opens fresh confirmation only. Native vector-quantization equivalence must be reported; it precludes Mirror-specific novelty if outputs match.
failure_gate: FAIL if either low-residual gate misses in either seed or if native vector quantization exactly matches the Mirror codebook without a separate Mirror-specific benefit.
boundaries: This tests code storage on synthetic latent-cluster functions, not decoder capacity; θ is frozen and identical.
No capacity claim from latent address combinatorics; assess held-out query and interpolation quality.
High-residual tasks expose when private full latent state becomes necessary.
Fresh remains sealed unless both development seeds pass.
